readingMode: Full sequential native reading, including index/introduction and page-crossing measures; original cover inspected visually. No annex beyond page29.

coverage.authoredAnalysis: Original cover visually inspected: Teruel Existe, general elections2023. Native extraction contains only the page number. No promise attributed to cover.
Fourteen-topic index and territorial introduction explicitly place this programme in Congress and Senate. Scope is Teruel; not all Spain Vaciada lists.

Introduction dated July2023 expressly names23July and Cortes Generales. Retrospective electoral/parliamentary success and useful-vote claims are campaign rhetoric, not neutral measures or verified achievements.

Introduction continues: infrastructure, public services, rural housing, energy and territorial inequality. Past interventions and cause/effect assertions are not independently established; final request explicitly addresses Teruel Congress/Senate candidates.

Institutional programme: territorial/rural budgeting, democratic dialogue, critical education and a Congress disinformation study. State finances actual minimum welfare-service costs considering dispersion/density; regions finance enhancements. Progressive capacity-based taxation and anti-fraud resources, no exact rate.

Local financing reform for towns below2,000people; transparency and direct election of provincial/comarcal representatives. Aragón autonomy/historical-debt and actual-cost financing. Operating aid in counties below12.5inhabitants/km²; no blanket national corporate reduction.

Climate/energy:2030emission goal,2050neutrality, vulnerable-consumer protection, local storage and citizen energy communities. Criticism of current large renewable deployment is qualified support for a different model. Household efficiency aid continues on page8.

Complete efficiency target:700,000homes per year with30%rural. Moratorium on large renewable parks and very-high-voltage lines for planning, local compensation and levy;20%transport-node access reserved for small installations. Distributed generation, self-consumption and energy communities expressly supported. Climate-law/substation reforms continue on page9.

Completes climate-law instruments and access of smaller investors to auctions; Nudo Mudéjar industrial/rail redevelopment. Environmental assessments for renewable/mining projects, resource/circular-economy policies and protected spaces. Sustainability rhetoric is not a measured impact guarantee.

Completes protected-space discussion; landscape policies, rural stewardship/forestry/extensive livestock and carbon capture. Water framework protection and explicit rejection of Ebro transfer projects. Water-supply condition finishes here: adequate good-quality supply without compromising resources.

Drought plans, saving/reuse/separate drainage and environmental education. Aragón Water Pact adapted to climate/reserves/ecological flows; reservoirs/irrigation conditioned on social, ecological and economic sustainability. Teruel river/dam/Andorra projects, riverbank care and irrigation-community renewables; Ebro lifting into Andorra should not be collapsed into opposition to every water movement.

Rural State pact with stable finance. In depopulated areas, towns below5,000: low/middle-income residents/owners may obtain IBI exemption and80%property-transfer-tax reduction for housing; State replaces local forgone IBI. Entrepreneurship/social economy and100/30/30plan;100megas is informal here, speed clarified on page24.

100/30/30continuation: basic public services within30minutes; high-capacity transport access within30kilometres, examples railway stop/autovía. Financial access/multi-bank ATMs, public agency decentralisation, Correos functions, pay supplement for hard-to-fill rural public jobs; rental-linked rehabilitation/protected rural housing, no exact nationwide rent cap.

Rural participation/women/employment/telework, EU territorial funds, maximum operating aid in Teruel and low-density Huesca/Zaragoza counties below12.5inhabitants/km². Starts public universal healthcare pact; does not reject all private healthcare.

Primary care financing25%of healthcare budget and rural access. Programme assertion that primary care can solve90%of health problems is not independent evidence. Professional management/training, nationwide usable electronic records, waiting-list bottlenecks and cancer screening. Rural staff recruitment/conditions continues page16.

Completes rural staff/MIR/vacation coverage. National services include mental/oral health and24/7urgent transport brought inside the national health system, coordinated with regions; no specified dental treatment basket or universal medical nationalisation. Public indicators. Social/dependency/equality section continues page17.

Education/vocational network and older-person neighbourhood/home-based care, loneliness/meal services. Public/protected housing including rural public rental and efficiency/accessibility rehabilitation; no general price cap stated. Equality/conciliation telework and shared household care begins.

Equal work/pay and targeted access for carers; explicit surrogacy rejection. Rural women entrepreneurship, lactation leave extended until one year with accumulated-hour use; distinguish from one-year paid parental leave. Youth emancipation, home support/flexible time and0-3education without explicit universal-free wording here. Gender-violence pact and LGTBI/racial/gender equality.

Rural chapter: depopulation/livestock-loss figures and causal narrative are programme assertions. Stewardship/extensive livestock support, rural-impact assessment mechanism and professional farming/fair prices/research; modernising food-chain value continues page20.

Family/extensive livestock favoured over macrofarms and differentiated family-agriculture law; food/forestry research/biosecurity. CAP equality and current production rather than historical sowing reference. Year-round fire prevention/extinction resources and technology; no fixed financial allocation.

Rural Civil Guard resources/barracks/housing, law45/2007update and stable demographic policy; cultural/natural heritage, local resources and collective woodland legal reform. Transport chapter begins territorial road mesh, completed page22.

Road mesh/regional integration and provincial-road modernisation; detailed A68/A40/Teruel-Requena-Almansa/A25projects. Named national-road bypasses; avoid representing a list of local constructions as a general rail-versus-road exclusion.

Completes bypass/road works. Modern conventional railway for every province and integrated AVE network; mixed passenger/freight double electrified Zaragoza-Teruel-Sagunto corridor, Platea intermodal/access and branch lines. No rail project cost or implementation deadline inferred.

Public rail/road rural mobility and on-demand transport; immediate direct Teruel-Madrid train and regional frequency/long-distance restoration; recover bus lines/stops. Digital access specifies minimum100Mbps symmetric in rural areas and fibre nodes under20km; regulatory assertions not independently certified. Fibre/alternative systems continues page25.

Completes fibre/access and5Gcoverage, digital training/accessible e-administration/security. Claimed50%rural5Ggap is source background. Science based on evidence, parliamentary science and supplementary talent-attraction/conciliation aid in depopulated provinces; continues page26.

Completes science/talent aid and internationalisation; university presence/degrees/research, territorial science priorities, libraries/festivals/cultural tourism/geoparks. No university tuition/free-access or quantified science budget proposal established.

Specific Aragón science centres/observatory and a national dinosaur-research centre. Rural manufacturing/local raw-material processing, logistics/circular economy and dispersal of publicly aided companies; attracts qualified workers, no guaranteed employment outcomes.

Repeats maximum low-density business aid; rural self-employed/shared premises, active employment policy/social economy. Small local-market shops/bars in towns below200qualify as social economy; no automatic subsidy amount. Rural tourism/LEADERfinance. FITEincrease continues page29.

FITEtarget90million euros, correcting stagnant allocation since2005and prioritising strategic investments rather than ordinary regional spending; amount period not separately specified. North Teruel industrial park, Andorra transition jobs and value-added/local food/quality brands. Final page has blank lower area; no further annex/notes.
